title: Implement LSP semantic tokens (full-document) for apexls
description:
## What
Add LSP `textDocument/semanticTokens/full` support to apexls-server, so editors get binder-grade semantic highlighting (fields vs. locals vs. static calls vs. unresolved) instead of TextMate-guess syntax coloring. This is the #1 priority gap in `.scratch/apex-lsp-gaps/research.md` (section 3, item 1).

## Where
All code changes are in exactly two files:

1. `crates/apexls-server/src/lib.rs` -- follow the pattern of `Backend::document_highlight` at line 1087 verbatim: snapshot `documents.version`, `wait_for_rebuild`, read `bind.program`, delegate to `capabilities::semantic_tokens_full(program, file, encoding)`. Add the `semantic_tokens_full` handler on the `LanguageServer` impl. Declare `semantic_tokens_provider` in `ServerCapabilities` in `Backend::initialize` (starting ~line 669). Emit the exact same `SemanticTokensLegend` your walker consumes -- keep it in one `const`/`fn` and reuse it in both the capability declaration and the walker so they can't drift.

2. `crates/apexls-server/src/capabilities.rs` -- add `pub(crate) fn semantic_tokens_full(program: &BoundProgram, file: FileId, encoding: PositionEncoding) -> SemanticTokens` next to the other capability functions (see `document_highlights` at line 653 or `folding_ranges` at line 703 as reference shape). This function walks `apex-binder`'s `SymbolTable`/`Resolution` data for `file`, produces sorted-by-position tokens, and LSP-delta-encodes them (`deltaLine`, `deltaStart`, `length`, `tokenType`, `tokenModifiers`).

## Token legend (start narrow, expand later)
Pick a minimal-but-useful subset of the LSP standard `SemanticTokenType`s that maps cleanly to what `apex-binder`'s `Resolution`/`SymbolKind` already distinguishes. Suggested v1:
- Types: `class`, `interface`, `enum`, `type` (fallback), `typeParameter`
- Callables: `method`, `function` (bare-call / trigger)
- Values: `property` (Apex field / SObject field), `variable` (local), `parameter`, `enumMember`
- Other: `namespace` (System, Schema, etc.), `keyword` only if you emit one for annotations (`@isTest`, `@AuraEnabled`)

Modifiers: `static`, `readonly` (for `final` locals + immutable stdlib fields), `declaration` (on the defining occurrence), `deprecated` (if binder tracks it -- else skip), `defaultLibrary` (for stdlib symbols).

Do NOT invent custom token types -- clients only theme the standard set reliably.

## Data source
`apex-binder` already classifies every identifier occurrence: see `crates/apex-binder/src/symbol.rs` (`SymbolKind`, `ModifierSet`), `crates/apex-binder/src/resolve.rs` (per-reference resolutions), and how `capabilities::document_highlights` / `capabilities::references` already walk the binder for occurrences. You are producing the token list from resolved-reference data that already exists; no new binder pass is needed. If some fine-grained detail truly isn't available, drop that token rather than adding a binder pass -- v1 explicitly favors coverage-over-fidelity.

## Encoding
LSP semantic tokens are delta-encoded: emit tokens sorted by (line, start), then encode each as 5 u32s relative to the previous token. Respect the negotiated `PositionEncoding` via `line_index` -- same helper the other capability functions already use to convert offsets to LSP positions.

## Explicitly OUT of scope for this task
- `textDocument/semanticTokens/range` -- do NOT implement; v1 is full-document only. The `semantic_tokens_provider.range` field stays `Some(false)` (or absent).
- `textDocument/semanticTokens/full/delta` -- do NOT implement; the `full.delta` field stays `Some(false)` (or absent). Return `SemanticTokens { result_id: None, data: [...] }`.
- No changes to `apex-binder`, `apex-parser`, `apex-syntax`, `apex-metadata`, `apex-stdlib`. If you find yourself needing to add a field to the binder for a token you want to emit, drop the token -- v1 uses only data that already exists.

## Acceptance
- `cargo check -p apexls-server` passes.
- `cargo clippy -p apexls-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- `ServerCapabilities` returned from `initialize` includes a populated `semantic_tokens_provider` with the same legend the walker uses.
- The handler follows the `wait_for_rebuild` + `bind.program` pattern used by every other capability handler in `lib.rs`.
- Inline unit tests in `capabilities.rs` (small `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`) cover: (a) delta-encoding of two tokens on the same line, (b) delta-encoding across lines, (c) a stdlib-static-member call emits `defaultLibrary` modifier, (d) a local variable reference emits `variable` (not `property`).

A separate QA task (created after this) adds an integration test through the LSP transport; do NOT add that integration test in this task.

title: Integration test for LSP semantic tokens over the transport
description:
## What
Add a new integration test file at `crates/apexls-server/tests/semantic_tokens.rs` that drives the LSP server end-to-end (initialize -> didOpen -> `textDocument/semanticTokens/full`) and asserts the returned tokens for a small representative Apex source.

## Pattern to follow
Use the same in-memory LSP-client harness the other integration tests in `crates/apexls-server/tests/` already use. Good references:
- `crates/apexls-server/tests/references_highlight.rs` -- same request/response shape and version-wait handling.
- `crates/apexls-server/tests/inlay_hints.rs` -- same `textDocument/*Provider` capability negotiation pattern.
- `crates/apexls-server/tests/handshake.rs` -- if you need to assert `semantic_tokens_provider` shows up in the `InitializeResult.capabilities`.

Do NOT invent a new test harness -- reuse whatever the existing files import.

## Coverage (keep it tight, one or two Apex fixtures)
Assert on the *decoded* token stream (undo the LSP delta-encoding for readability of the assertion), not the raw u32 list. At minimum verify:
1. `initialize` response includes `semantic_tokens_provider` with a non-empty legend and `full = true`.
2. For a small Apex class fixture (a class with: one field, one method, one local variable, one call to a stdlib type e.g. `System.debug(...)`, one reference to a user-defined type), `textDocument/semanticTokens/full` returns tokens whose positions and token types match what the fixture expects (e.g. the field identifier tokenizes as `property`, the local as `variable`, the `System` in `System.debug` as `namespace` or the stdlib call carries the `defaultLibrary` modifier).
3. A negative check: an unresolved identifier does NOT crash and either gets no token or a fallback token type -- the server must not return an error, must not panic, and must not deadlock.

## Do NOT
- Do not add golden fixture files under `tests/golden/` -- integration tests here are inline. If you need multi-line Apex source, use a raw string literal in the test file.
- Do not modify `crates/apexls-server/src/lib.rs`, `capabilities.rs`, or any binder crate -- that is the implement task's territory. If a test surfaces a real bug in the implementation, mark the test `#[ignore]` with a comment describing the bug and open a follow-up ticket rather than editing the implementation from here.

## Acceptance
- `cargo test -p apexls-server --test semantic_tokens` passes.
- `cargo clippy -p apexls-server --tests -- -D warnings` passes.
- File exists at exactly `crates/apexls-server/tests/semantic_tokens.rs` (one file, no submodules).
